disclaimer: PilSim is a research simulator, not a clinical decision support tool. These rules encode published contraindications, interactions and guideline preferences so that a virtual-patient simulation behaves plausibly. They are incomplete by construction, have not been validated against any patient population, and must never be used to make or withhold a prescribing decision for a real person.
scope_note: Rules are written for the five modeled substances only: lisinopril, losartan, amlodipine, hydrochlorothiazide, metoprolol. Interacting partners outside that set (NSAIDs, lithium, simvastatin, CYP inhibitors, aliskiren, sacubitril/valsartan) are represented as drug_class atoms so the engine can flag them if the user adds a co-medication, without those drugs being modeled pharmacokinetically.

substance_gating_contract.rule: MANDATORY FOR ALL CONSUMERS. Any effect carrying a `substance` key applies ONLY when that substance is actually present in the regimen. A rule's trigger firing is NOT sufficient authority to apply every effect it contains.
substance_gating_contract.why: Several rules are deliberately multi-substance - their trigger is an `any` over drugs that share an adverse-effect class. AE-CHANNELS-VISIBLE fires on lisinopril OR amlodipine OR hydrochlorothiazide, but carries per-drug cough, angioedema, oedema and skin-cancer figures. Without gating, a hydrochlorothiazide-only regimen inherits lisinopril's cough and angioedema numbers with FDA citations attached, pointing at a drug the patient is not taking. That is a citation-integrity failure, not just a scoring bug.
also_gate_on: `applies_to` (array of substance ids, used by score_delta)
`applies_to_partner` (the interacting drug, used by pk_multiply in the CYP rules)
`requires_salt` (used by CI-HFREF-METOPROLOL-SUCCINATE for succinate_er vs tartrate)
`when` (named condition string, used by the dose-adjustment rules)
substance_gating_contract.legitimate_exception: Rules whose trigger is an `all` over two substances are COMBINATION rules - the harm arises from the pairing, not from either drug. Their effects are regimen-level and correctly carry no `substance` key. DDI-BB-THIAZIDE-DYSGLYCEMIA is the only such rule in this file: its dysglycemia effects belong to metoprolol+hydrochlorothiazide together and must not be attributed to either alone. Distinguish these from `any`-triggered shared-channel rules, where gating is mandatory.
substance_gating_contract.audit_2026_08_17: Full sweep of all 48 rules for this failure mode. Found and fixed two further instances beyond the one reported: the two `annotate_organ` effects in AE-CHANNELS-VISIBLE were ungated, so a hydrochlorothiazide-only regimen would have animated amlodipine's capillary-leak oedema and an amlodipine-only regimen would have animated hydrochlorothiazide's photosensitivity. Also added explicit `substance` keys to the three `pk_multiply` effects in DOSE-HEPATIC-AMLODIPINE-LOSARTAN, which were previously self-gating only via their `pk.<substance>.*` target path. No remaining ungated effects except the documented combination-rule exception.

provenance_contract.rule: Every effect carrying a PHARMACOLOGICAL number (a PK/PD multiplier, a lab or vital shift, a risk, a dose in mg, a titration interval) has a `provenance` field: either a citation object {source,url,quote,type,retrieved} or the literal string "ESTIMATED" plus `estimate_basis`.
provenance_contract.deliberate_exception: `score_delta.delta` values carry NO provenance and are not pharmacological claims. They are design weights for the ranking objective in research/05-OUTPUT-REPORT-SPEC.md and are owned by Agent F. They are on an arbitrary scale where -100 means disqualifying and +35 means a strong guideline-backed preference. Do not cite them as evidence of anything.
provenance_contract.honesty_note: The ESTIMATED count is high and that is the truthful state of this domain. Regulatory labels overwhelmingly describe interaction DIRECTION without magnitude. Where a magnitude is asserted without a source it is flagged, and the flagged items are listed in research/C-notes.md section 4.

organ_binding.note: annotate_organ organ ids are aligned to Agent F's element ids in research/04-ORGAN-EFFECT-MAP.md section 13.1. Reconciled 2026-08-17 after F flagged a conflict. That conflated upper-airway swelling with lower-airway smooth-muscle constriction - different anatomy, mechanism, timescale and clinical urgency. elements.lung.airway: Lower-airway bronchial smooth muscle, beta-2 or hypersensitivity mediated. Emitted by RX-ASTHMA-METOPROLOL, RX-COPD-METOPROLOL-NO-CARDIAC-INDICATION, EXC-AZO-DYE. Uses the calibre-narrowing animation.

organ_binding.direction_convention: down = suppressed (F tints blue, calibre index below 1.00); up = increased (F tints red, calibre index above 1.00).

renal_function_contract.note: Reconciled with Agent D 2026-08-17. All rules in this file key on `labs.egfr_ml_min_1_73`, the BSA-INDEXED value from the 2021 race-free CKD-EPI creatinine equation (which replaced both the 2009 race-coefficient equation and MDRD).
renal_function_contract.use_indexed_for: Guideline thresholds - the eGFR 60 / 30 / 15 cutpoints in CI-ALBUMINURIA-RAASI, DOSE-RENAL-LISINOPRIL and EFF-HCTZ-ADVANCED-CKD are all guideline numbers and use the indexed value.
renal_function_contract.use_deindexed_for: Drug clearance scaling inside the PK model. De-index by multiplying by BSA/1.73 per the 2025 National Kidney Foundation consensus. Agent E must apply this when converting eGFR to a clearance term - the pk_multiply factor in DOSE-RENAL-LISINOPRIL assumes de-indexed clearance.
renal_function_contract.cockcroft_gault: Display-only. FDA's 2024 renal impairment guidance and NKF have both moved off it, but FDA LABELS still express renal dose bands in Cockcroft-Gault creatinine clearance. DOSE-RENAL-LISINOPRIL therefore quotes CrCl bands (>30, 10-30, <10) because that is what the label says, while the trigger atom uses eGFR. Treat them as approximately interchangeable for the simulation and disclose the approximation in the UI.

demo_gate_rule_ids.comment: The four locked reject cases plus the locked drug-drug reject, by stable id, for Agents E and F to bind against.

rules.title: ACE inhibitor in pregnancy
rules.mechanism: Fetal renal perfusion depends on angiotensin II from the second trimester onward; blocking its formation collapses fetal urine output, causing oligohydramnios, pulmonary hypoplasia, skull hypoplasia, limb contractures, anuria and death.

effects.reason: Absolute contraindication — FDA boxed warning for fetal toxicity.

effects.estimate_basis: Used as a categorical UI flag, not an incidence estimate; the label states injury and death 'can' result and gives no incidence.

warning.short: Never in pregnancy — fetal injury and death
warning.full: Lisinopril carries an FDA boxed warning: drugs that act directly on the renin-angiotensin system can cause injury and death to the developing fetus. It must be discontinued as soon as pregnancy is detected. The older teaching that first-trimester exposure is safe is not current labeling.

evidence.source: FDA label, ZESTRIL (lisinopril) — BOXED WARNING: FETAL TOXICITY
evidence.quote: When pregnancy is detected, discontinue ZESTRIL as soon as possible. Drugs that act directly on the renin-angiotensin system can cause injury and death to the developing fetus.

evidence.source: 2025 AHA/ACC/multisociety High Blood Pressure Guideline, Circulation 2025;152:e114-e218
evidence.quote: Contraindicated in pregnancy: atenolol, ACE inhibitors, ARBs, direct renin inhibitors, nitroprusside, mineralocorticoid receptor antagonists.

rules.title: ARB in pregnancy
rules.mechanism: Angiotensin II receptor blockade removes the AT1-mediated drive to fetal renal perfusion and glomerular filtration, producing the same oligohydramnios / fetal renal failure sequence as ACE inhibition.

effects.reason: Absolute contraindication — FDA boxed warning for fetal toxicity.

effects.estimate_basis: Categorical UI flag; label gives no incidence.

warning.short: Never in pregnancy — fetal injury and death
warning.full: Losartan carries an FDA boxed warning for fetal toxicity. Discontinue as soon as pregnancy is detected. ARBs are contraindicated in pregnancy for the same reason as ACE inhibitors — the fetal kidney depends on angiotensin II signalling.

evidence.source: FDA label, COZAAR (losartan potassium) — BOXED WARNING: FETAL TOXICITY
evidence.quote: When pregnancy is detected, discontinue COZAAR as soon as possible. Drugs that act directly on the renin-angiotensin system can cause injury and death to the developing fetus.

evidence.source: 2025 AHA/ACC/multisociety High Blood Pressure Guideline
evidence.quote: Contraindicated in pregnancy: ... ACE inhibitors, ARBs, direct renin inhibitors ...

rules.title: Thiazide in pregnancy — avoid, not absolute
rules.mechanism: Thiazides reduce plasma volume, and pregnancy already depends on plasma-volume expansion for placental perfusion; volume contraction is theoretically linked to impaired fetal growth, and thiazides also cross the placenta and can cause fetal/neonatal electrolyte disturbance and thrombocytopenia.

effects.reason: Not first-line in pregnancy; a pregnancy-appropriate agent should be substituted.

warning.short: Avoid in pregnancy — not a first-line agent
warning.full: Hydrochlorothiazide is not an absolute contraindication in pregnancy the way ACE inhibitors and ARBs are, but it is not among the recommended agents. Pregnancy-appropriate antihypertensives are labetalol, extended-release nifedipine and methyldopa.

evidence.source: 2025 AHA/ACC/multisociety High Blood Pressure Guideline — pregnancy section
evidence.quote: Chronic hypertension in pregnancy: treat to <140/90 mm Hg; contraindicated agents are atenolol, ACE inhibitors, ARBs, direct renin inhibitors, nitroprusside and MRAs.

rules.title: ACE inhibitor with prior angioedema
rules.mechanism: ACE (kininase II) degrades bradykinin; inhibiting it raises bradykinin, and patients who have already had ACE-inhibitor angioedema have a markedly higher chance of a recurrent, potentially airway-obstructing episode on re-exposure.

effects.reason: Labeled contraindication — history of angioedema with an ACE inhibitor.

effects.estimate_basis: Recurrence on rechallenge is substantially higher than the 0.1-0.7% first-exposure rate; no single labeled RR exists, so 10x is a flagged placeholder for the UI risk bar.

warning.short: Prior ACE-inhibitor angioedema — do not rechallenge
warning.full: A history of angioedema associated with previous ACE inhibitor treatment, and hereditary or idiopathic angioedema, are labeled contraindications to lisinopril. An ARB may be considered but is not risk-free.

evidence.source: FDA label, ZESTRIL (lisinopril), CONTRAINDICATIONS
evidence.quote: ZESTRIL is contraindicated in patients with a history of angioedema or hereditary or idiopathic angioedema.

rules.title: Hydrochlorothiazide in anuria
rules.mechanism: Hydrochlorothiazide acts from the tubular lumen on the NCC cotransporter in the distal convoluted tubule; with no urine flow the drug never reaches its target and only accumulates.

provenance.source: Mechanistic — no tubular flow, no luminal drug delivery
provenance.quote: Hydrochlorothiazide is contraindicated in patients with anuria.

warning.short: Contraindicated in anuria
warning.full: Hydrochlorothiazide is contraindicated in anuria — it cannot reach its luminal target in the distal convoluted tubule.

evidence.source: FDA label, hydrochlorothiazide tablets USP (DailyMed), CONTRAINDICATIONS
evidence.quote: Anuria. Hypersensitivity to this product or other sulfonamide-derived drugs.

rules.title: Hydrochlorothiazide with sulfonamide hypersensitivity
rules.mechanism: Hydrochlorothiazide is a sulfonamide derivative; the label treats hypersensitivity to other sulfonamide-derived drugs as a contraindication, although true immunological cross-reactivity between non-antibiotic and antibiotic sulfonamides is now considered uncommon.

warning.short: Sulfonamide hypersensitivity — contraindicated
warning.full: The hydrochlorothiazide label contraindicates use in hypersensitivity to sulfonamide-derived drugs. Note the clinical nuance: cross-reactivity between antibiotic sulfonamides and non-antibiotic sulfonamides such as thiazides is far weaker than the label implies, but PilSim follows the label.

evidence.source: FDA label, hydrochlorothiazide tablets USP (DailyMed), CONTRAINDICATIONS
evidence.quote: Hypersensitivity to this product or other sulfonamide-derived drugs.

rules.title: Metoprolol with conduction disease, shock or decompensated heart failure
rules.mechanism: Beta-1 blockade slows sinus node firing and AV nodal conduction and reduces contractility, which in a patient already dependent on sympathetic drive for rate or output precipitates complete block, profound bradycardia or circulatory collapse.

effects.reason: Labeled contraindication for metoprolol succinate ER.

effects.estimate_basis: Illustrative magnitude for the blocked-run preview animation; not a label value.

warning.short: Conduction disease / shock / decompensated HF — contraindicated
warning.full: Metoprolol succinate ER is contraindicated in severe bradycardia, second- or third-degree heart block, cardiogenic shock, decompensated cardiac failure, and sick sinus syndrome unless a permanent pacemaker is in place.

evidence.source: FDA label, metoprolol succinate extended-release tablets (DailyMed), CONTRAINDICATIONS
evidence.quote: Metoprolol succinate extended-release tablets are contraindicated in severe bradycardia, second or third degree heart block, cardiogenic shock, decompensated cardiac failure, sick sinus syndrome (unless a permanent pacemaker is in place), and in patients who are hypersensitive to any component of this product.

rules.title: Metoprolol before alpha blockade in pheochromocytoma
rules.mechanism: Blocking beta-2-mediated vasodilatation in skeletal muscle while catecholamine-driven alpha-1 vasoconstriction is unopposed produces a paradoxical rise in blood pressure — the 'unopposed alpha' effect.

effects.reason: Beta blockade without prior alpha blockade in pheochromocytoma.

effects.estimate_basis: Directionally correct illustrative magnitude for the paradoxical pressor response; the label describes the effect qualitatively.

warning.short: Pheochromocytoma — alpha blocker first
warning.full: In pheochromocytoma, metoprolol may only be given after an alpha blocker has been started. Beta blockade alone causes a paradoxical increase in blood pressure.

evidence.source: FDA label, metoprolol succinate ER (DailyMed), WARNINGS AND PRECAUTIONS — Pheochromocytoma
evidence.quote: If metoprolol succinate extended-release is used in the setting of pheochromocytoma, it should be given in combination with an alpha blocker, and only after the alpha blocker has been initiated. Administration of beta-blockers alone in the setting of pheochromocytoma has been associated with a paradoxical increase in blood pressure due to the attenuation of beta-mediated vasodilatation in skeletal muscle.

rules.title: Lactose-containing product in galactosaemia / congenital lactase deficiency / glucose-galactose malabsorption
rules.mechanism: Lactose is hydrolysed to glucose and galactose; in the rare hereditary defects of galactose handling or intestinal monosaccharide transport, even excipient-scale galactose is not safely disposed of.

effects.reason: Choose a lactose-free formulation of the same active ingredient.

warning.short: Contains lactose — avoid in rare hereditary sugar disorders
warning.full: This product contains lactose. Patients with rare hereditary problems of galactose intolerance, total lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption should not take it. A lactose-free formulation of the same active ingredient should be substituted.

evidence.source: Annex to the European Commission guideline on 'Excipients in the labelling and package leaflet of medicinal products for human use' (SANTE-2017-11668), EMA/CHMP/302620/2017 Rev.1, 22 Nov 2019 — Lactose entry, oral route, threshold zero
evidence.quote: SmPC proposal: Patients with rare hereditary problems of galactose intolerance, total lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption should not take this medicine.

rules.title: Ordinary lactose intolerance is NOT a contraindication to a lactose-containing tablet
rules.mechanism: The lactose dose delivered by oral solid dosage forms is one to two orders of magnitude below the symptom threshold for adult-type hypolactasia, so it is almost never the cause of symptoms.

warning.short: Lactose present, but the dose is far below the symptom threshold
warning.full: This product contains lactose as an excipient. Daily lactose exposure from medicines is unlikely to exceed about 2 g, whereas the symptom threshold in adult-type lactose intolerance is around 12 g (roughly 250 mL of milk). Ordinary lactose intolerance is therefore not a reason to reject this product; only the rare hereditary disorders are. This rule exists to stop the safety engine from producing a false positive.

evidence.source: NHS Specialist Pharmacy Service — Assessing the clinical impact of lactose in medicines
evidence.quote: Daily exposure from medicines is unlikely to exceed 2g per day ... the threshold for lactose intolerance symptoms is approximately 12g (equivalent to 250ml of milk).

rules.title: Azo colourant (tartrazine / FD&C Yellow No. 5) sensitivity
rules.mechanism: Azo colourants can provoke non-immunological allergic-type reactions including urticaria and bronchospasm in susceptible people, disproportionately those with aspirin hypersensitivity.

effects.estimate_basis: 21 CFR describes the association qualitatively and states overall population sensitivity is low; no incidence figure is given, so 2x is a flagged placeholder for the risk bar.

warning.short: Contains an azo dye — allergic-type reactions possible
warning.full: This product contains FD&C Yellow No. 5 (tartrazine) or another azo colourant, which may cause allergic-type reactions including bronchial asthma in susceptible persons. Sensitivity is uncommon overall but is frequently seen in patients who also have aspirin hypersensitivity. A dye-free formulation should be preferred.

evidence.source: 21 CFR 201.20 — Declaration of presence of FD&C Yellow No. 5 and/or FD&C Yellow No. 6 in certain drugs for human use
evidence.quote: This product contains FD&C Yellow No. 5 (tartrazine) which may cause allergic-type reactions (including bronchial asthma) in certain susceptible persons. Although the overall incidence of FD&C Yellow No. 5 (tartrazine) sensitivity in the general population is low, it is frequently seen in patients who also have aspirin hypersensitivity.

evidence.source: EMA excipients annex (SANTE-2017-11668) Rev.1 — Azo colouring agents, oral, threshold zero
evidence.quote: Azo colouring agents — Oral — Zero — May cause allergic reactions. e.g.: Tartrazine (E 102), Sunset yellow FCF (E 110), Azorubine, carmoisine (E 122), Amaranth (E 123), Ponceau 4R, cochineal Red A (E 124), Brilliant black BN, black PN (E 151)

rules.title: High excipient sodium content in a patient on a low-sodium diet or with heart failure / CKD
rules.mechanism: Sodium delivered as an excipient adds to dietary sodium load, expanding extracellular volume and directly opposing the antihypertensive and decongestive effect of the regimen.

effects.estimate_basis: 391 mg sodium is ~20% of the WHO 2 g/day maximum; a ~10% attenuation of BP response is a directionally reasonable placeholder, not a measured value.

warning.short: High sodium content for a low-salt patient
warning.full: The maximum daily dose of this product delivers 391 mg (17 mmol) of sodium or more, which the EMA classifies as 'high' sodium content — about 20% of the WHO recommended maximum daily intake of 2 g sodium for an adult. Prefer a low-sodium formulation in patients advised to follow a low-salt diet. Note: a product delivering less than 1 mmol (23 mg) sodium per dose is 'essentially sodium-free'.

evidence.source: EMA excipients annex (SANTE-2017-11668) Rev.1 — Sodium entry
evidence.quote: 17 mmol (391 mg) is approximately 20% of the WHO adult recommended maximum daily dietary intake of 2 g sodium and is considered to represent 'high' sodium. ... This medicine contains less than 1 mmol sodium (23 mg) per <dosage unit>, that is to say essentially 'sodium-free'. 1 mmol of sodium (Na) = 23 mg Na = 58.4 mg salt (NaCl).

rules.title: Sodium contributed by the salt form of the active ingredient
rules.mechanism: Sodium salts of actives and of disintegrants such as croscarmellose sodium and sodium starch glycolate contribute a small but declarable sodium load.

warning.short: Contains declarable sodium
warning.full: This product contains 23 mg (1 mmol) of sodium or more per dose and must be declared. At this level the contribution is small relative to dietary intake but should be counted for patients on a strict sodium restriction.

evidence.source: EMA excipients annex (SANTE-2017-11668) Rev.1 — Sodium, oral/parenteral, threshold 1 mmol (23 mg) per dose
evidence.quote: This medicine contains x mg sodium (main component of cooking/table salt) in each <dosage unit>. This is equivalent to y% of the recommended maximum daily dietary intake of sodium for an adult.

rules.title: Dual RAAS blockade — ACE inhibitor plus ARB
rules.mechanism: Blocking angiotensin II formation and AT1 signalling simultaneously removes both arms of glomerular efferent arteriolar tone and of aldosterone-driven potassium excretion, so filtration pressure and potassium handling fail together without any added organ-protective benefit.

effects.reason: Label instruction: in general, avoid combined use of RAS inhibitors.

effects.estimate_basis: No trial reports a mean serum-potassium delta for dual blockade; they report event rates instead (see risk_set below). 0.2-0.8 mmol/L is a flagged modelling estimate sized to produce the observed excess of threshold-crossing events.

provenance.source: Fried LF et al., VA NEPHRON-D — Combined Angiotensin Inhibition for the Treatment of Diabetic Nephropathy, N Engl J Med 2013;369:1892-1903
provenance.quote: Combination therapy increased the risk of hyperkalemia (6.3 events per 100 person-years, vs. 2.6 events per 100 person-years with monotherapy; P<0.001) and acute kidney injury (12.2 vs. 6.7 events per 100 person-years, P<0.001).

provenance.source: VA NEPHRON-D, N Engl J Med 2013;369:1892-1903
provenance.quote: acute kidney injury (12.2 vs. 6.7 events per 100 person-years, P<0.001)

provenance.source: Parving HH et al., ALTITUDE — Cardiorenal End Points in a Trial of Aliskiren for Type 2 Diabetes, N Engl J Med 2012;367:2204-2213
provenance.quote: hyperkalemia (serum potassium level, >=6 mmol per liter) was significantly higher in the aliskiren group than in the placebo group (11.2% vs. 7.2%), as was the proportion with reported hypotension (12.1% vs. 8.3%) (P<0.001 for both)
provenance.note: ALTITUDE tested aliskiren added to an ACEi or ARB, so this is the triple-blockade upper bound, not the ACEi+ARB figure. Use it as a ceiling.

effects.estimate_basis: Dual RAAS blockade adds little BP effect because both agents act on the same pathway; ~10% incremental effect is the modelling assumption and is deliberately small.

warning.short: Do not combine an ACE inhibitor with an ARB
warning.full: Combining lisinopril with losartan is dual blockade of the renin-angiotensin system. It increases hypotension, hyperkalemia and acute kidney injury without additional renal or cardiovascular benefit. In VA NEPHRON-D, adding lisinopril to losartan in type 2 diabetes with albuminuria produced no benefit and more hyperkalemia and acute kidney injury. The two agents act at adjacent points in the same cascade, so their blood-pressure effects are largely redundant.

evidence.source: FDA label, lisinopril tablets (Aurobindo, DailyMed) §7.4 Dual Blockade of the Renin-Angiotensin System
evidence.quote: Dual blockade of the RAS with angiotensin receptor blockers, ACE inhibitors, or aliskiren is associated with increased risks of hypotension, hyperkalemia, and changes in renal function (including acute renal failure) compared to monotherapy. ... Patients receiving the combination of losartan and lisinopril did not obtain any additional benefit compared to monotherapy for the combined endpoint of decline in GFR, end state renal disease, or death, but experienced an increased incidence of hyperkalemia and acute kidney injury compared with the monotherapy group. In general, avoid combined use of RAS inhibitors.

evidence.source: FDA label, losartan potassium tablets (DailyMed) §7.4
evidence.quote: Dual blockade of the RAS with angiotensin receptor blockers, ACE inhibitors, or aliskiren is associated with increased risks of hypotension, syncope, hyperkalemia, and changes in renal function (including acute renal failure) compared to monotherapy.

rules.title: Aliskiren with an ACE inhibitor or ARB in diabetes
rules.mechanism: Adding a direct renin inhibitor to ACE or AT1 blockade is the most complete form of RAAS shutdown and in diabetes produced excess renal impairment, hyperkalemia, hypotension and stroke without benefit.

effects.reason: Labeled contraindication — aliskiren co-administered with an ACE inhibitor in patients with diabetes.

warning.short: Aliskiren + ACEi/ARB in diabetes — contraindicated
warning.full: Co-administration of aliskiren with lisinopril in patients with diabetes is a labeled contraindication. Aliskiren must also be avoided with lisinopril in renal impairment (GFR < 60 mL/min).

evidence.source: FDA label, lisinopril tablets (DailyMed) — CONTRAINDICATIONS and §7.4
evidence.quote: Do not co-administer aliskiren with lisinopril in patients with diabetes. Avoid use of aliskiren with lisinopril in patients with renal impairment (GFR <60 mL/min).

rules.title: ACE inhibitor within 36 hours of sacubitril/valsartan
rules.mechanism: Neprilysin and ACE are the two main bradykinin-degrading enzymes; inhibiting both at once allows bradykinin to accumulate and sharply raises the risk of life-threatening angioedema.

effects.reason: Labeled contraindication — combination with a neprilysin inhibitor; 36-hour washout required.

effects.estimate_basis: Label states increased angioedema risk without a ratio; 3x is a flagged placeholder for the UI risk bar.

warning.short: 36-hour washout required with sacubitril/valsartan
warning.full: Lisinopril is contraindicated in combination with a neprilysin inhibitor. Do not administer lisinopril within 36 hours of switching to or from sacubitril/valsartan — the overlap risks severe angioedema.

evidence.source: FDA label, lisinopril tablets (DailyMed) §4 CONTRAINDICATIONS
evidence.quote: Lisinopril tablets are contraindicated in combination with a neprilysin inhibitor (e.g., sacubitril). Do not administer lisinopril tablets within 36 hours of switching to or from sacubitril/valsartan, a neprilysin inhibitor.

rules.title: RAAS inhibitor with potassium-sparing diuretic, potassium supplement or potassium salt substitute
rules.mechanism: RAAS inhibition removes aldosterone-driven potassium secretion in the collecting duct while the co-administered agent adds a potassium load or blocks the same secretory step, so serum potassium rises additively.

effects.estimate_basis: Label names the risk factors but gives no delta; range chosen to be clinically plausible and is flagged as an estimate.
Directional placeholder; no labeled ratio.

warning.short: Hyperkalemia risk — avoid extra potassium
warning.full: Risk factors for hyperkalemia on a RAAS inhibitor include renal insufficiency, diabetes mellitus, and concomitant use of potassium-sparing diuretics, potassium supplements or potassium-containing salt substitutes. The 2025 AHA/ACC guideline endorses potassium-based salt substitutes for sodium reduction but specifically cautions against them in CKD or on drugs that reduce potassium excretion — this rule is that caution made machine-readable.

evidence.source: FDA label, lisinopril tablets (DailyMed) §5.5 Hyperkalemia
evidence.quote: Risk factors for the development of hyperkalemia include renal insufficiency, diabetes mellitus, and the concomitant use of potassium-sparing diuretics, potassium supplements and/or potassium-containing salt substitutes.

evidence.source: 2025 AHA/ACC/multisociety High Blood Pressure Guideline
evidence.quote: Potassium-based salt substitutes should be used with caution in patients with CKD or those taking medications that reduce potassium excretion; monitor serum potassium.

rules.title: Triple whammy — RAAS inhibitor + diuretic + NSAID
rules.mechanism: The NSAID removes prostaglandin-mediated afferent arteriolar dilation, the RAAS inhibitor removes angiotensin II-mediated efferent constriction, and the diuretic removes the volume that was sustaining renal perfusion — all three determinants of glomerular filtration pressure fail at once.

provenance.source: Lapi F et al., nested case-control study of triple therapy and acute kidney injury, BMJ 2013
provenance.quote: current use of triple therapy (ACE inhibitor/ARB, diuretic and an NSAID) was associated with an increased rate of acute kidney injury (Rate Ratio 1.31, 95% CI 1.12-1.53) compared to double therapy; the greatest risk was in the first 30 days of use (Rate Ratio 1.82, 95% CI 1.35-2.46)

effects.provenance: Same source as above — the first-30-day rate ratio. Apply this value for simulated days 0-30 and 1.31 thereafter.

effects.estimate_basis: No labeled or trial eGFR delta exists for the triad; -8 mL/min/1.73m2 is a modelling choice sized to be visible but non-catastrophic, flagged as an estimate.

warning.short: Triple whammy — acute kidney injury risk
warning.full: A RAAS inhibitor plus a diuretic plus an NSAID is the classic 'triple whammy'. Rate ratio for acute kidney injury is 1.31 versus dual therapy overall and 1.82 in the first 30 days. The lisinopril/HCTZ and losartan/HCTZ fixed-dose combinations already supply two of the three legs, so a single over-the-counter NSAID completes the triad.

evidence.source: FDA label, lisinopril tablets (DailyMed) §7.3
evidence.quote: In patients who are elderly, volume-depleted (including those on diuretic therapy), or with compromised renal function, coadministration of NSAIDs, including selective COX-2 inhibitors, with ACE inhibitors, including lisinopril, may result in deterioration of renal function, including possible acute renal failure.

evidence.source: Kidney International — combined NSAID + diuretic and/or RAS inhibitor use and AKI risk
evidence.quote: Rate Ratio 1.31 (95% CI 1.12-1.53) for triple therapy vs double therapy; 1.82 (1.35-2.46) in the first 30 days.

rules.title: NSAIDs attenuate the antihypertensive effect of ACE inhibitors and ARBs
rules.mechanism: NSAIDs block renal prostaglandin synthesis, promoting sodium retention and vasoconstriction that directly opposes RAAS-inhibitor-mediated blood pressure reduction.

effects.estimate_basis: The label states attenuation qualitatively; a 30% loss of BP effect is a modelling assumption in the range commonly reported for NSAID-induced BP rise (3-5 mmHg on a ~10 mmHg effect).
As above.

warning.short: NSAID blunts the blood-pressure effect
warning.full: The antihypertensive effect of ACE inhibitors and ARBs may be attenuated by NSAIDs including selective COX-2 inhibitors. If blood pressure control is lost after starting an NSAID, this is the likely cause.

evidence.source: FDA label, losartan potassium tablets (DailyMed) §7.3
evidence.quote: The antihypertensive effect of angiotensin II receptor antagonists, including losartan, may be attenuated by NSAIDs, including selective COX-2 inhibitors.

rules.title: ACE inhibitor or ARB with lithium
rules.mechanism: Lithium is handled like sodium in the proximal tubule; drugs that promote sodium loss increase proximal lithium reabsorption and raise serum lithium into the toxic range.

effects.estimate_basis: Label describes toxicity without a numeric rise; +0.3 mmol/L on a 0.6-1.0 therapeutic range is a flagged modelling estimate.

warning.short: Lithium toxicity risk — monitor levels
warning.full: Lithium toxicity has been reported with ACE inhibitors and ARBs. Monitor serum lithium during concurrent use; the effect is usually reversible on stopping both.

evidence.source: FDA label, lisinopril tablets (DailyMed) §7.5 Lithium
evidence.quote: Lithium toxicity has been reported in patients receiving lithium concomitantly with drugs, which cause elimination of sodium, including ACE inhibitors. Lithium toxicity was usually reversible upon discontinuation of lithium and the ACE inhibitor. Monitor serum lithium levels during concurrent use.

rules.title: Hydrochlorothiazide with lithium
rules.mechanism: Thiazide-induced volume contraction increases proximal tubular reabsorption of sodium and, with it, lithium — reducing renal lithium clearance.

effects.estimate_basis: Label states thiazides reduce lithium renal clearance and adds a high risk of toxicity; a 25% clearance reduction is a flagged modelling estimate consistent with the qualitative warning.
As above.

warning.short: Lithium generally should not be given with diuretics
warning.full: The hydrochlorothiazide label states that lithium generally should not be given with diuretics. Thiazides reduce renal lithium clearance and add a high risk of lithium toxicity.

evidence.source: FDA label, hydrochlorothiazide tablets USP (DailyMed) WARNINGS / PRECAUTIONS — Drug Interactions
evidence.quote: Lithium generally should not be given with diuretics (see PRECAUTIONS, Drug Interactions).

rules.title: Hydrochlorothiazide with digoxin — hypokalemia-potentiated toxicity
rules.mechanism: Thiazide-induced potassium loss reduces competition with digoxin at the Na+/K+-ATPase binding site, so the same digoxin concentration produces greater inhibition and greater ventricular irritability.

effects.estimate_basis: Label describes sensitisation qualitatively; 2x is a flagged placeholder for the risk bar.

warning.short: Hypokalemia sensitises the heart to digitalis
warning.full: Hypokalemia may cause cardiac arrhythmia and may also sensitize or exaggerate the response of the heart to the toxic effects of digitalis, including increased ventricular irritability. Monitor potassium.

evidence.source: FDA label, hydrochlorothiazide tablets USP (DailyMed) PRECAUTIONS
evidence.quote: Hypokalemia may cause cardiac arrhythmia and may also sensitize or exaggerate the response of the heart to the toxic effects of digitalis (e.g., increased ventricular irritability).

rules.title: Metoprolol in asthma — caution, NOT an absolute contraindication
rules.mechanism: Beta-1 selectivity is relative, not absolute; at higher plasma concentrations metoprolol also blocks airway beta-2 receptors, removing the sympathetic bronchodilator tone that asthmatic airways depend on.

effects.reason: Use only if the patient does not respond to or cannot tolerate other antihypertensive treatment; use the lowest possible dose and keep a bronchodilator available.

provenance.source: Morales DR et al., Chest 2014;145:779-786 — acute cardioselective beta-blockers in asthma
provenance.quote: Acute selective beta-blockers in the doses given caused a mean change in FEV1 of -6.9% (95% CI, -8.5 to -5.2), a fall in FEV1 of >=20% in one in eight patients (P=.03)
a mean change in FEV1 of -6.9% (95% CI, -8.5 to -5.2)
a fall in FEV1 of >=20% in one in eight patients

warning.short: Asthma — avoid unless no alternative; keep a bronchodilator ready
warning.full: Asthma is NOT listed in the metoprolol CONTRAINDICATIONS section — it is a Warning (5.3 Bronchospastic Disease). The label says patients with bronchospastic disease should in general not receive beta-blockers, but that metoprolol may be used in those who do not respond to or cannot tolerate other treatment, at the lowest possible dose, with bronchodilators available. Acute cardioselective beta-blockade drops FEV1 by about 6.9% on average, with a fall of 20% or more in roughly one in eight asthmatic patients. Non-selective beta-blockers such as propranolol ARE absolutely contraindicated in bronchial asthma — do not generalise metoprolol's status to the whole class, or the class's status to metoprolol.

evidence.source: FDA label, metoprolol succinate ER (DailyMed) §4 CONTRAINDICATIONS — full text
evidence.quote: Metoprolol succinate extended-release tablets are contraindicated in severe bradycardia, second- or third-degree heart block, cardiogenic shock, decompensated heart failure, sick sinus syndrome (unless a permanent pacemaker is in place), and in patients who are hypersensitive to any component of this product.
evidence.note: Asthma does not appear. Verified independently on the TOPROL-XL brand label (rev. Feb 2025, DailyMed setid 496ddfaa-7c9c-4888-b747-a210249b367a) and four current generics.

evidence.source: FDA label, metoprolol succinate ER (DailyMed) §5.3 Bronchospastic Disease
evidence.quote: Patients with bronchospastic diseases should, in general, not receive beta-blockers. Because of its relative beta 1 cardio-selectivity, however, metoprolol succinate extended-release tablets may be used in patients with bronchospastic disease who do not respond to, or cannot tolerate, other antihypertensive treatment. Because beta 1-selectivity is not absolute, use the lowest possible dose of metoprolol succinate extended-release tablets. Bronchodilators, including beta 2-agonists, should be readily available or administered concomitantly.

evidence.source: FDA label, INDERAL LA (propranolol), ANI Pharmaceuticals rev. 06/2024 — CONTRAINDICATIONS (contrast case)
evidence.quote: Propranolol is contraindicated in 1) cardiogenic shock; 2) sinus bradycardia and greater than first-degree block; 3) bronchial asthma; and 4) in patients with known hypersensitivity to propranolol hydrochloride.

evidence.source: Huang KY et al., Sci Rep 2021;11:452 — network meta-analysis of 24 RCTs
evidence.quote: In participants with a baseline asthma history, in addition to oral timolol and infusion of propranolol, oral labetalol, oxprenolol, propranolol, and metoprolol exhibited significantly higher incidences of asthma attack than did the placebo.

rules.title: Metoprolol in COPD without a cardiac indication
rules.mechanism: In COPD without a cardiovascular indication, beta-1 blockade offers no offsetting cardiac benefit while still reducing airway sympathetic tone and blunting the response to beta-2 agonist rescue therapy.

provenance.source: Dransfield MT et al., BLOCK COPD — Metoprolol for the Prevention of Acute Exacerbations of COPD, N Engl J Med 2019;381:2304-2314
provenance.quote: hospitalization for an exacerbation during treatment was more common among patients in the metoprolol group (hazard ratio 1.91; 95% CI, 1.29 to 2.83)

provenance.source: Cochrane / Salpeter-type meta-analysis of cardioselective beta-blockers in COPD, as sourced by Agent D (see research/02-VIRTUAL-HUMAN.md)
provenance.quote: cardioselective beta-1 blockade reduces FEV1 by about 2.05% (95% CI -6.05 to +1.96) in COPD and does not worsen with continued use
provenance.note: Confidence interval crosses zero - the COPD spirometric effect of a cardioselective agent is not statistically distinguishable from none. Contrast the ASTHMA figure of -6.9% (95% CI -8.5 to -5.2), which does not cross zero. This is why asthma and COPD are separate rules.

warning.short: COPD without a cardiac indication — do not add a beta-blocker
warning.full: Cardioselective beta-blockers should not be withheld from COPD patients who have a cardiovascular indication for them. But BLOCK-COPD randomised COPD patients WITHOUT such an indication to metoprolol and found more hospitalisation for exacerbation (HR 1.91, 95% CI 1.29-2.83). The BICS trial of bisoprolol in COPD (n=515) was neutral rather than harmful, so this signal may be metoprolol- or design-specific. Either way, do not start metoprolol in COPD purely to lower blood pressure — use one of the four first-line classes instead.

evidence.source: Dransfield MT et al., N Engl J Med 2019;381:2304-2314 (BLOCK COPD)
evidence.quote: Metoprolol ... hospitalization for an exacerbation was more common (hazard ratio 1.91; 95% CI, 1.29 to 2.83).

evidence.source: BICS — bisoprolol in COPD, JAMA 2024; n=515 (bisoprolol 261 / placebo 258)
evidence.quote: serious adverse events 14.5% vs 14.3% (RR 1.01, 0.62-1.66)

rules.title: Hydrochlorothiazide in gout or hyperuricemia
rules.mechanism: Thiazide-induced volume contraction increases proximal tubular urate reabsorption via URAT1 and OAT4, raising serum urate and precipitating crystal deposition and acute gout flares.

effects.reason: Switch to a non-urate-raising antihypertensive where feasible; losartan is the preferred substitute in this drug set.

effects.estimate_basis: A per-dose mg/dL urate rise for HCTZ could not be sourced at label or open-access level (Peterzan 2012 full text is paywalled and gives only a potency ordering). +0.8 mg/dL at 25 mg is a flagged modelling estimate; scale linearly with dose over 12.5-50 mg. SEE C-notes.md gap list.
Directional placeholder; no labeled or single agreed ratio was retrieved.

warning.short: Thiazide raises urate — avoid in gout
warning.full: Thiazides raise serum urate and can precipitate gout. Note the nuance for the audit: hyperuricemia and gout are NOT contraindications in the hydrochlorothiazide label — the label's only contraindications are anuria and sulfonamide hypersensitivity. The reject strength comes from the gout guideline literature, which conditionally favours switching hydrochlorothiazide when feasible, not from regulatory labeling. PilSim treats it as a relative contraindication with an override.

evidence.source: FDA label, hydrochlorothiazide tablets USP (DailyMed) — CONTRAINDICATIONS section, full text
evidence.quote: Anuria. Hypersensitivity to this product or other sulfonamide-derived drugs.
evidence.note: Gout is absent from the contraindications; hyperuricemia appears only as a precaution.

evidence.source: Cochrane review of thiazide metabolic effects (PMID 24869750)
evidence.quote: Thiazides reduced potassium, increased uric acid and increased total cholesterol and triglycerides ... changes were dose-related and were least for hydrochlorothiazide.

rules.title: CYP2D6 poor metabolizer on metoprolol
rules.mechanism: Metoprolol is cleared almost entirely by CYP2D6 alpha-hydroxylation and O-demethylation; with no functional enzyme, clearance collapses, exposure rises several-fold and beta-1 selectivity is lost as concentrations climb.

provenance.source: CPIC Guideline for CYP2D6, ADRB1, ADRB2, ADRA2C, GRK4, and GRK5 Genotypes and Beta-Blocker Therapy (Duarte JD et al., Clin Pharmacol Ther, 2024, doi:10.1002/cpt.3351, PMID 38951961)
provenance.quote: more than a two-fold longer elimination half-life, with a nearly five-fold increase in area under the plasma concentration-time curve (AUC)
The mean elimination half-life of metoprolol is 3 to 4 hours; in poor CYP2D6 metabolizers the half-life may be 7 to 9 hours.
approximately 3-8 beats/min greater heart rate reduction
approximately 3-6 mmHg systolic; 2-6 mmHg diastolic greater blood pressure reduction

provenance.source: CPIC 2024 beta-blocker guideline, Table 2, CYP2D6 poor metabolizer
provenance.quote: Initiate therapy with lowest recommended starting dose. Carefully titrate dose upward to clinical effect or guideline-recommended dose; monitor more closely for bradycardia. Alternatively, consider selecting another beta-blocker.

effects.estimate_basis: CPIC advises closer bradycardia monitoring in PMs but gives no incidence ratio; 2x is a flagged placeholder.

warning.short: CYP2D6 poor metabolizer — start low, titrate slowly
warning.full: CYP2D6 poor metabolizers have roughly a five-fold higher metoprolol AUC and a half-life of 7-9 hours instead of 3-4. CPIC (2024, moderate strength) advises starting at the lowest recommended dose, titrating carefully, and monitoring for bradycardia, or choosing a different beta-blocker. CPIC also notes that a poor metabolizer already stable on a well-tolerated regimen probably does not need a change on genotype alone. CYP2D6 is absent in about 8% of Caucasians and about 2% of most other populations.

evidence.source: FDA label, metoprolol succinate ER (DailyMed) §12.5 Pharmacogenomics
evidence.quote: CYP2D6 is absent in about 8% of Caucasians (poor metabolizers) and about 2% of most other populations. CYP2D6 can be inhibited by several drugs. Poor metabolizers of CYP2D6 will have increased (several-fold) metoprolol blood levels, decreasing metoprolol's cardioselectivity.

evidence.source: CPIC Guideline for CYP2D6 and Beta-Blocker Therapy, 2024
evidence.quote: Poor metabolizer (activity score 0): Initiate therapy with lowest recommended starting dose ... Moderate classification of recommendation.

rules.title: CYP2D6 intermediate, normal or ultrarapid metabolizer on metoprolol — standard dosing
rules.mechanism: Residual CYP2D6 activity above an activity score of zero is sufficient to keep metoprolol exposure within the range for which standard dosing was established.

effects.estimate_basis: CPIC recommends standard dosing for IM and gives no IM-specific AUC ratio; 1.6x is a flagged interpolation between NM (1.0) and PM (~4.9) and must not be presented as a guideline value.

provenance.quote: Normal metabolizer (activity score 1.25-2.25): Initiate standard dosing. Strong classification of recommendation.

warning.short: Standard metoprolol dosing
warning.full: CPIC 2024 recommends standard metoprolol dosing for CYP2D6 normal metabolizers (strong) and intermediate metabolizers (moderate). For ultrarapid metabolizers CPIC makes NO recommendation, citing insufficient evidence about diminished effectiveness — PilSim must not invent a dose increase for UM patients.

evidence.source: CPIC Guideline for CYP2D6 and Beta-Blocker Therapy, 2024, Table 2
evidence.quote: Ultrarapid metabolizer (>2.25): No recommendation for metoprolol therapy due to insufficient evidence regarding diminished metoprolol effectiveness clinically.

rules.title: Metoprolol with a strong CYP2D6 inhibitor (phenoconversion)
rules.mechanism: Strong CYP2D6 inhibitors such as quinidine, fluoxetine, paroxetine and propafenone convert a normal metabolizer into a functional poor metabolizer, doubling or more metoprolol concentrations and eroding beta-1 selectivity.

provenance.source: FDA label, metoprolol succinate ER (DailyMed) §7.2 CYP2D6 Inhibitors
provenance.quote: Drugs that are strong inhibitors of CYP2D6 such as quinidine, fluoxetine, paroxetine, and propafenone were shown to double metoprolol concentrations.
propafenone 150 mg t.i.d. with immediate-release metoprolol 50 mg t.i.d. resulted in steady state concentration of metoprolol 2- to 5-fold what is seen with metoprolol alone

assume a CYP2D6 activity score of zero (i.e., poor metabolizer) in patients taking adequate doses of a concomitant strong CYP2D6 inhibitor and to reduce the predicted activity score by half in patients taking a moderate inhibitor. No activity score adjustment is suggested for weak inhibitors.

effects.estimate_basis: Label states selectivity decreases with rising concentration but gives no ratio; 0.6 is a flagged modelling choice that feeds the asthma/COPD risk channel.
Directional placeholder proportional to the doubled exposure.

warning.short: Strong CYP2D6 inhibitor doubles metoprolol levels
warning.full: Quinidine, fluoxetine, paroxetine and propafenone at least double metoprolol concentrations; propafenone raises steady-state levels 2- to 5-fold. Rising concentrations reduce metoprolol's beta-1 selectivity, which matters most in a patient with asthma or COPD. Per CPIC 2024, treat such a patient as a functional CYP2D6 poor metabolizer; halve the predicted activity score for a moderate inhibitor.

evidence.source: FDA label, metoprolol succinate ER (DailyMed) §7.2
evidence.quote: Drugs that are strong inhibitors of CYP2D6 such as quinidine, fluoxetine, paroxetine, and propafenone were shown to double metoprolol concentrations. While there is no information about moderate or weak inhibitors, these too are likely to increase metoprolol concentration. Increases in plasma concentration decrease the cardioselectivity of metoprolol. Monitor patients closely when the combination cannot be avoided.

rules.title: Metoprolol with a non-dihydropyridine CCB, digoxin or clonidine
rules.mechanism: Beta blockade and non-dihydropyridine calcium channel blockade or digitalis each slow sinoatrial firing and atrioventricular conduction by independent mechanisms, so their effects on rate and conduction are additive.

effects.estimate_basis: Label describes additive bradycardia without a numeric delta; -12 bpm is a flagged modelling estimate on top of the metoprolol-alone effect.
Directional placeholder; no labeled ratio.

warning.short: Additive bradycardia and AV block
warning.full: Digitalis glycosides, clonidine, diltiazem and verapamil slow atrioventricular conduction and decrease heart rate; combining them with metoprolol increases the risk of bradycardia. Note that the label names bradycardia and slowed AV conduction only — AV block and hypotension are not named in this interaction section, though they follow from the same mechanism.

evidence.source: FDA label, metoprolol succinate ER (DailyMed) §7.3
evidence.quote: Digitalis glycosides, clonidine, diltiazem and verapamil slow atrioventricular conduction and decrease heart rate. Concomitant use with beta blockers can increase the risk of bradycardia.

rules.title: Abrupt discontinuation of metoprolol
rules.mechanism: Chronic beta blockade upregulates beta-adrenergic receptors; sudden withdrawal exposes the sensitised myocardium to unopposed catecholamine drive, precipitating rebound tachycardia, angina and infarction.

effects.estimate_basis: Label describes rebound qualitatively; +15 bpm over 48 h is a flagged modelling estimate to make the withdrawal animation visible.
Directional placeholder; label reports the events without a rate.

warning.short: Taper over 1-2 weeks — never stop abruptly
warning.full: Following abrupt cessation of beta-blockade, exacerbations of angina and in some cases myocardial infarction have occurred. Reduce the dose gradually over 1 to 2 weeks and monitor. Because coronary artery disease is common and may be unrecognized, avoid abrupt discontinuation even in patients treated only for hypertension.

evidence.source: FDA label, metoprolol succinate ER (DailyMed) §5.1 Abrupt Cessation of Therapy
evidence.quote: When discontinuing chronically administered metoprolol succinate extended-release tablets, particularly in patients with ischemic heart disease, gradually reduce the dosage over a period of 1 - 2 weeks and monitor the patient. ... Because coronary artery disease is common and may be unrecognized, avoid abruptly discontinuing metoprolol succinate extended-release tablets in patients treated only for hypertension.

rules.title: Metoprolol masking hypoglycemia in insulin- or sulfonylurea-treated diabetes
rules.mechanism: The adrenergic warning symptoms of hypoglycemia — chiefly tachycardia and tremor — are beta-mediated, so beta blockade removes the patient's cue to treat a falling glucose, and beta-2 blockade also blunts hepatic glycogenolytic recovery.

effects.estimate_basis: Label states the risk qualitatively; 2x is a flagged placeholder for the risk bar.
Modelling choice representing loss of the tachycardia cue while sweating is preserved; flagged as an estimate.

warning.short: Masks hypoglycemia warning signs
warning.full: Beta-blockers may prevent early warning signs of hypoglycemia such as tachycardia, and increase the risk of severe or prolonged hypoglycemia, especially in diabetes and in patients who are fasting or vomiting. Sweating is generally preserved. This is a monitoring and patient-education rule, not a contraindication.

evidence.source: FDA label, metoprolol succinate ER (DailyMed) §5.7 Hypoglycemia
evidence.quote: Beta-blockers may prevent early warning signs of hypoglycemia, such as tachycardia, and increase the risk for severe or prolonged hypoglycemia at any time during treatment, especially in patients with diabetes mellitus or children and patients who are fasting (i.e., surgery, not eating regularly, or are vomiting).

rules.title: Amlodipine with a CYP3A inhibitor
rules.mechanism: Amlodipine is cleared by CYP3A-mediated oxidation; inhibiting that pathway raises systemic exposure, deepening arteriolar vasodilation into symptomatic hypotension and prerenal kidney injury.

provenance.source: FDA label, amlodipine besylate tablets (DailyMed) §12.3 CYP3A inhibitors
provenance.quote: Coadministration of a 180 mg daily dose of diltiazem with 5 mg amlodipine in elderly hypertensive patients resulted in a 60% increase in amlodipine systemic exposure.

effects.estimate_basis: The FDA label explicitly declines to quantify strong CYP3A inhibitors ('may increase the plasma concentrations of amlodipine to a greater extent' than diltiazem's 60%). 2.0x is a flagged modelling choice sitting above the measured diltiazem value. No labeled clarithromycin or itraconazole AUC ratio exists — do not present one as sourced.

provenance.source: Gandhi S et al., Calcium-Channel Blocker-Clarithromycin Drug Interactions and Acute Kidney Injury, JAMA 2013;310(23):2544-2553 (amlodipine-specific OR as quoted in the Health Canada amlodipine monograph)
provenance.quote: odds ratio amlodipine: 1.61 (95% C.I. 1.29-2.02); overall AKI 0.44% clarithromycin vs 0.22% azithromycin, OR 1.98 (1.68-2.34)

effects.estimate_basis: Scaled to the exposure increase; the JAMA 2013 hypotension OR of 1.60 is for all CCBs pooled, not amlodipine alone.

warning.short: CYP3A inhibitor raises amlodipine exposure
warning.full: Co-administration with moderate or strong CYP3A inhibitors increases amlodipine exposure and may require a dose reduction. Diltiazem 180 mg raised amlodipine exposure by 60%; strong inhibitors such as itraconazole and clarithromycin raise it further, though the label gives no number. In older adults, clarithromycin added to amlodipine roughly doubled 30-day acute kidney injury risk. Erythromycin and grapefruit juice do NOT significantly change amlodipine exposure — the common grapefruit warning does not apply to this drug.

evidence.source: FDA label, amlodipine besylate tablets (DailyMed) §12.3
evidence.quote: Coadministered cimetidine, magnesium- and aluminum hydroxide antacids, sildenafil, and grapefruit juice have no impact on the exposure to amlodipine. ... Erythromycin coadministration in healthy volunteers did not significantly change amlodipine systemic exposure. However, strong inhibitors of CYP3A (e.g., itraconazole, clarithromycin) may increase the plasma concentrations of amlodipine to a greater extent.

rules.title: Simvastatin dose cap on amlodipine
rules.mechanism: Amlodipine is a weak CYP3A inhibitor and raises simvastatin exposure, and simvastatin myopathy and rhabdomyolysis are concentration-dependent.

provenance.quote: Limit the dose of simvastatin in patients on amlodipine to 20 mg daily.

provenance.source: FDA label, amlodipine besylate tablets (DailyMed) §12.3; concordant with the ZOCOR label PK table (simvastatin AUC ratio 1.77, Cmax 1.47)
provenance.quote: Coadministration of multiple doses of 10 mg of amlodipine with 80 mg simvastatin resulted in a 77% increase in exposure to simvastatin compared to simvastatin alone.

effects.estimate_basis: Scaled to the 1.77x exposure increase; no labeled myopathy ratio for this pair.

warning.short: Cap simvastatin at 20 mg/day with amlodipine
warning.full: Amlodipine 10 mg raises simvastatin exposure by 77%. Do not exceed simvastatin 20 mg daily in a patient taking amlodipine. This is a genuine dose-cap rule the simulator's titration search must respect, not just a warning.

evidence.source: FDA label, NORVASC (amlodipine) Highlights and §7.7
evidence.quote: Do not exceed doses greater than 20 mg daily of simvastatin. (7.7)

evidence.source: FDA label, ZOCOR (simvastatin) §2.5
evidence.quote: Patients taking Amiodarone, Amlodipine, or Ranolazine - Do not exceed ZOCOR 20 mg once daily.

rules.title: Losartan with fluconazole or another CYP2C9 inhibitor
rules.mechanism: Losartan is a prodrug-like agent whose antihypertensive work is done mostly by E-3174, formed primarily by CYP2C9; inhibiting CYP2C9 traps drug as the weaker parent and reduces the active metabolite.

provenance.source: FDA label, losartan potassium tablets (DailyMed) — Drug Interactions
provenance.quote: Fluconazole, an inhibitor of cytochrome P450 2C9, decreased the AUC of the active metabolite by approximately 40%, but increased the AUC of losartan by approximately 70% following multiple doses.
decreased the AUC of the active metabolite by approximately 40%

effects.estimate_basis: E-3174 is 10-40x more potent by weight than losartan, so a 40% loss of metabolite is only partly offset by a 70% rise in parent; a 25% net efficacy loss is a flagged modelling estimate. The label states 'The pharmacodynamic consequences of concomitant use of losartan and inhibitors of P450 2C9 have not been examined.'

warning.short: CYP2C9 inhibition cuts the active metabolite by ~40%
warning.full: Fluconazole decreases the AUC of losartan's active metabolite E-3174 by about 40% while increasing parent losartan AUC by about 70%. Since E-3174 is 10 to 40 times more potent by weight, net antihypertensive effect is expected to fall. The label explicitly states the pharmacodynamic consequence has not been examined, so PilSim's efficacy penalty here is a modelling assumption.

evidence.source: FDA label, losartan potassium tablets (DailyMed) — Drug Interactions
evidence.quote: Conversion of losartan to its active metabolite after intravenous administration is not affected by ketoconazole, an inhibitor of P450 3A4. The AUC of active metabolite following oral losartan was not affected by erythromycin, an inhibitor of P450 3A4, but the AUC of losartan was increased by 30%.

evidence.source: FDA label, COZAAR (losartan) Clinical Pharmacology — E-3174 potency
evidence.quote: About 14% of an orally-administered dose of losartan is converted to the active metabolite. ... The active metabolite is 10 to 40 times more potent by weight than losartan ... the conversion of losartan to its active metabolite is mediated primarily by P450 2C9 and not P450 3A4.

rules.title: Losartan with rifampin (CYP2C9/3A4 induction)
rules.mechanism: Rifampin induces the enzymes that both form and further clear losartan and E-3174, and the net effect is faster elimination of both, so total active exposure falls.

provenance.quote: rifampin has been shown to decrease the AUC of losartan and its active metabolite by 30% and 40%, respectively.
decrease the AUC of losartan and its active metabolite by 30% and 40%, respectively

effects.estimate_basis: Tracks the 40% loss of the dominant active moiety; flagged as an estimate.

warning.short: Rifampin cuts losartan exposure by 30-40%
warning.full: Rifampin decreases the AUC of losartan by 30% and of its active metabolite by 40%. Expect loss of blood pressure control; consider an alternative agent or higher monitoring frequency during rifampin therapy.

evidence.source: FDA label, losartan potassium tablets (DailyMed)
evidence.quote: rifampin has been shown to decrease the AUC of losartan and its active metabolite by 30% and 40%, respectively.

rules.title: CYP2C9 poor metabolizer on losartan
rules.mechanism: CYP2C9*3/*3 homozygotes convert little losartan to E-3174, so the patient is exposed mainly to the 10-40x weaker parent compound.

effects.estimate_basis: No clean percentage reduction in E-3174 AUC by genotype could be sourced. Yasar 2002 reports the losartan:E-3174 AUC ratio is 30-fold higher in CYP2C9*3/*3; 0.4 is a flagged modelling choice, deliberately conservative. There is NO CPIC and NO DPWG guideline for CYP2C9 and losartan — verified against both registries.

Sekino 2003 found SBP/DBP fell in *1/*1 but not *1/*3 carriers; Bae 2012 found no difference for heterozygotes, and a 2021 meta-analysis found the effect significant in Asians but not Caucasians. The evidence is genuinely conflicting — flagged low confidence.

warning.short: CYP2C9 poor metabolizer — losartan may work less well
warning.full: CYP2C9*3/*3 homozygotes form far less E-3174 and may get less blood pressure lowering from losartan. Evidence is conflicting for heterozygotes and there is no CPIC or DPWG pharmacogenomic guideline for this pair, so PilSim treats this as a low-confidence modifier and not an actionable dosing rule. Do not present it to a judge as guideline-backed personalization the way the CYP2D6/metoprolol rule can be.

evidence.source: Yasar U et al., Clin Pharmacol Ther 2002 (PMID 11823761)
evidence.quote: The ratio of the total losartan AUC to the total E-3174 AUC was higher in the subject with the CYP2C9*3/*3 genotype (30-fold) and also in the CYP2C9*1/*3 and *2/*3 groups (approximately 2- and 3-fold, respectively) compared with the CYP2C9*1/*1 group.

evidence.source: Bae JW et al. (PMID 22735459) — contradicting evidence for heterozygotes
evidence.quote: AUC0-inf of E-3174 was not different ... the clinical effects of losartan may not be reduced by CYP2C9*1/*3.

rules.title: Maximum daily doses for the five modeled substances
rules.mechanism: Above these doses the labels report either no additional efficacy or a disproportionate rise in adverse effects, so the simulator's dose-optimisation search must not propose them.

provenance.quote: The recommended initial dose is 10 mg once a day. ... The usual dosage range is 20 mg to 40 mg per day administered in a single daily dose. Doses up to 80 mg have been used but do not appear to give greater effect.
provenance.note: 80 mg is NOT a labeled maximum - the label mentions it only to say it gives no greater effect. Encode 40 mg.

provenance.quote: maximum dose of 100 mg once daily
The usual initial antihypertensive oral dose of amlodipine besylate tablets is 5 mg once daily, and the maximum dose is 10 mg once daily.

provenance.source: FDA label, hydrochlorothiazide tablets USP (DailyMed) DOSAGE AND ADMINISTRATION
provenance.quote: The usual initial dose in adults is 25 mg daily given as a single dose. The dose may be increased to 50 mg daily, given as a single or two divided doses. Doses above 50 mg are often associated with marked reductions in serum potassium.
Adults: The usual initial dosage is 25 to 100 mg daily in a single dose. ... Dosages above 400 mg per day have not been studied.
In general, wait 7 to 14 days between titration steps.
Adjust dosage at weekly (or longer) intervals until optimum blood pressure reduction is achieved. In general, the maximum effect of any given dosage level will be apparent after 1 week of therapy.

warning.short: Labeled maximum daily doses
warning.full: Lisinopril 40 mg, losartan 100 mg, amlodipine 10 mg, hydrochlorothiazide 50 mg (12.5-25 mg is the modern antihypertensive range), metoprolol succinate ER 400 mg (200 mg in heart failure). The dose-optimisation search must not exceed these.

evidence.source: See per-effect provenance blocks above — each cap is quoted from its own FDA label.
evidence.quote: See effects[].provenance

rules.title: Lisinopril renal dose adjustment
rules.mechanism: Lisinopril is not metabolised at all and is excreted entirely unchanged by the kidney, so its clearance falls in direct proportion to glomerular filtration and exposure accumulates.

provenance.quote: In patients with creatinine clearance >= 10 mL/min and <= 30 mL/min, reduce the initial dose of lisinopril tablets to half of the usual recommended dose i.e., hypertension, 5 mg ... Up titrate as tolerated to a maximum of 40 mg daily.
For patients on hemodialysis or creatinine clearance < 10 mL/min, the recommended initial dose is 2.5 mg once daily.

effects.estimate_basis: Set proportional to the eGFR ratio at the midpoint of the 10-30 mL/min band relative to a 90 mL/min reference; derived, not quoted.

warning.short: Halve the starting dose below CrCl 30
warning.full: No dose adjustment is required above CrCl 30 mL/min. At CrCl 10-30, halve the initial dose (5 mg for hypertension), titrating to a maximum of 40 mg daily. At CrCl below 10 or on hemodialysis, start at 2.5 mg once daily. KDIGO 2024 practice point 3.6.7 says to continue an ACEi or ARB even when eGFR falls below 30 — reduce the dose, do not reflexively stop the drug.

evidence.source: FDA label, lisinopril tablets (DailyMed) §2.4 Dose in Patients with Renal Impairment
evidence.quote: Renal Impairment: For patients with creatinine clearance >= 10 mL/min and <= 30 mL/min, halve usual initial dose. For patients with creatinine clearance < 10 mL/min or on hemodialysis, the recommended initial dose is 2.5 mg.

evidence.source: KDIGO 2024 Clinical Practice Guideline for the Evaluation and Management of CKD, Practice Point 3.6.7
evidence.quote: Continue ACEi or ARB in people with CKD even when the eGFR falls below 30 ml/min per 1.73 m2.

rules.title: Hepatic impairment and frailty dose reduction for amlodipine and losartan
rules.mechanism: Both amlodipine and losartan undergo substantial hepatic clearance and first-pass extraction; impaired liver function roughly doubles losartan bioavailability and prolongs amlodipine half-life to 56 hours, while ageing independently reduces amlodipine clearance.

provenance.quote: Small, fragile, or elderly patients, or patients with hepatic insufficiency may be started on 2.5 mg once daily and this dose may be used when adding amlodipine besylate tablets to other antihypertensive therapy.

Because amlodipine besylate is extensively metabolized by the liver and the plasma elimination half-life (t1/2) is 56 hours in patients with impaired hepatic function, titrate slowly when administering amlodipine besylate to patients with severe hepatic impairment.
provenance.note: 56 h vs a normal 30-50 h reference; factor derived from the quoted 56 h.

provenance.quote: Elderly patients have decreased clearance of amlodipine with a resulting increase of AUC of approximately 40-60%.
Use a starting dose of 25 mg for patients with mild to moderate hepatic impairment.
Compared to normal subjects the total plasma clearance of losartan in patients with hepatic insufficiency was about 50% lower and the oral bioavailability was about doubled.

warning.short: Start low in hepatic impairment, frailty or old age
warning.full: Amlodipine: start at 2.5 mg in small, fragile or elderly patients or hepatic insufficiency; elderly AUC is 40-60% higher and half-life reaches 56 hours in liver impairment. Losartan: start at 25 mg in mild-to-moderate hepatic impairment (clearance 50% lower, bioavailability roughly doubled) and in volume-depleted patients such as those already on a diuretic. Losartan has NOT been studied in severe hepatic impairment. Neither drug needs a renal dose reduction — amlodipine PK is not significantly influenced by renal impairment, and losartan needs no adjustment unless the patient is also volume depleted.

evidence.source: FDA label, NORVASC §12.3 — renal
evidence.quote: The pharmacokinetics of amlodipine are not significantly influenced by renal impairment. Patients with renal failure may therefore receive the usual initial dose.

rules.title: Hydrochlorothiazide at reduced kidney function — attenuated, NOT abolished
rules.mechanism: Less filtered sodium reaches the distal convoluted tubule and less thiazide is secreted into the lumen, so the natriuretic yield per milligram falls — but the NCC target remains present and responsive.

effects.estimate_basis: CLICK showed chlorthalidone still produced a 10.5 mmHg placebo-subtracted 24-h SBP fall at eGFR 15-30, i.e. comparable to normal-kidney effect sizes. A 25% attenuation is a deliberately conservative modelling choice; setting this to 0 would reproduce the team's outdated draft claim and would be wrong.

provenance.source: Agarwal R et al., Chlorthalidone for Hypertension in Advanced Chronic Kidney Disease, N Engl J Med 2021;385:2507-2519 (CLICK)
provenance.quote: hypokalemia 10% vs 0%; reversible creatinine rise >25% in 45% vs 13%
reversible creatinine rise >25% in 45% vs 13%
provenance.note: The +0.2 mg/dL magnitude is derived from the >25% threshold applied to a typical stage-4 baseline; the incidence is the quoted trial value.

warning.short: Still works at low eGFR — watch potassium and creatinine
warning.full: AUDIT CORRECTION. The claim that thiazides stop working at low kidney function is outdated. The CLICK trial randomised patients with stage 4 CKD (eGFR 15 to under 30) and uncontrolled hypertension to chlorthalidone or placebo, and found a placebo-subtracted 24-hour systolic fall of 10.5 mmHg (95% CI -14.6 to -6.4) at 12 weeks plus a 50-percentage-point greater fall in albuminuria. The real caveats are hypokalemia (10% vs 0%), a reversible creatinine rise above 25% (45% vs 13%), and that loop diuretics are preferred when the goal is volume removal rather than blood pressure. The standalone hydrochlorothiazide label sets no eGFR cutoff and no renal dose cap; the CrCl 30 figure comes from combination-product labeling.

evidence.source: Agarwal R et al., N Engl J Med 2021;385:2507-2519 (CLICK)
evidence.quote: 24-h ambulatory SBP change at 12 weeks: chlorthalidone -11.0 mm Hg (95% CI -13.9 to -8.1) vs placebo -0.5 (-3.5 to 2.5); between-group -10.5 mm Hg (95% CI -14.6 to -6.4), P<0.001.

evidence.source: FDA label, lisinopril and hydrochlorothiazide tablets (DailyMed) — the source of the CrCl 30 threshold
evidence.quote: need not be adjusted as long as the patient's creatinine clearance is greater than 30 mL/min/1.73 m2 ... In patients with more severe renal impairment, loop diuretics are preferred to thiazides.

rules.title: Four co-equal first-line antihypertensive classes
rules.mechanism: Randomised evidence shows blood pressure reduction itself, rather than any class-specific property, drives most of the cardiovascular benefit, so four classes qualify equally as first-line absent a compelling indication.

provenance.source: 2025 AHA/ACC/multisociety High Blood Pressure Guideline, Circulation 2025;152:e114-e218
provenance.quote: All patients without compelling indications should be initiated on a thiazide, angiotensin-converting enzyme inhibitor, angiotensin receptor blocker, or dihydropyridine calcium channel blocker.

provenance.source: 2024 ESC Guidelines for the management of elevated blood pressure and hypertension, Eur Heart J 2024;45:3912-4018
provenance.quote: ACE inhibitors or ARBs, dihydropyridine calcium channel blockers, and thiazide or thiazide-like diuretics are the recommended first line BP-lowering medications (Class I). While beta blockers are not considered as first line, they are recommended in combination with first line medications when there is a compelling indication (Class I).

warning.short: Thiazide, ACEi, ARB or DHP-CCB first — beta-blocker needs a reason
warning.full: For uncomplicated hypertension, prefer a thiazide-type diuretic, ACE inhibitor, ARB, or dihydropyridine calcium channel blocker. Metoprolol is NOT a first-line antihypertensive under either the 2025 AHA/ACC or the 2024 ESC guideline — it requires a compelling indication such as heart failure with reduced ejection fraction, prior myocardial infarction, angina or rate control in atrial fibrillation. AUDIT NOTE: the 2025 guideline also removed race-based first-line selection; all four classes now apply to all patients regardless of race or ethnicity.

evidence.source: 2025 AHA/ACC/multisociety High Blood Pressure Guideline
evidence.quote: Previous guidelines recommended calcium channel blockers or thiazides as first-line agents for Black patients; the updated guideline now recommends all 4 first-line classes for all patients, with individualized selection based on comorbidities and patient-specific factors rather than race.

rules.title: Prefer an ACE inhibitor or ARB in albuminuric CKD or diabetic kidney disease
rules.mechanism: Angiotensin II preferentially constricts the efferent arteriole; blocking it lowers intraglomerular pressure, which reduces albuminuria and slows nephron loss beyond what the same blood-pressure fall achieves by other means.

provenance.source: ADA Standards of Care in Diabetes-2026, Section 10, Recommendation 10.8
provenance.quote: ACE inhibitors or angiotensin receptor blockers (ARBs) are recommended first-line therapy for hypertension in people with diabetes and albuminuria or coronary artery disease. A

effects.estimate_basis: Placeholder hook so Agent E can attach an albuminuria-reduction term; no numeric multiplier is asserted here.

provenance.quote: In adults with hypertension and CKD, electrolytes should be checked 2-4 weeks after starting or intensifying ACEis or ARBs to check for hyperkalemia or an eGFR decrease >30%.

warning.short: Albuminuria — prefer an ACE inhibitor or ARB
warning.full: ACE inhibitors and ARBs are the preferred agents when albuminuria (UACR 30 mg/g or higher), eGFR under 60, or coronary artery disease is present. AUDIT CORRECTION: this preference is NOT general to all diabetes. The ADA states plainly that in the absence of albuminuria, ACE inhibitors and ARBs have not been found to afford superior cardioprotection compared with thiazide-like diuretics or dihydropyridine calcium channel blockers. Check electrolytes and eGFR 2-4 weeks after starting; a creatinine rise above 30% within 4 weeks is the KDIGO threshold for reconsidering the drug.

evidence.source: ADA Standards of Care in Diabetes-2026, Section 10, body text
evidence.quote: In the absence of albuminuria, risk of progressive kidney disease is low, and ACE inhibitors and ARBs have not been found to afford superior cardioprotection compared with thiazide-like diuretics or dihydropyridine calcium channel blockers.

evidence.source: KDIGO 2024 Clinical Practice Guideline for the Evaluation and Management of CKD, Recommendations 3.6.1-3.6.3
evidence.quote: 3.6.1 We recommend starting renin-angiotensin-system inhibitors (RASi) (ACEi or ARB) for people with CKD and severely increased albuminuria (G1-G4, A3) without diabetes (1B). 3.6.3 We recommend starting RASi for people with CKD and moderately-to-severely increased albuminuria (G1-G4, A2 and A3) with diabetes (1B).

evidence.source: KDIGO 2024, Practice Point 3.6.4
evidence.quote: Continue ACEi or ARB therapy unless serum creatinine rises by more than 30% within 4 weeks following initiation or dose increase.

rules.title: Prefer losartan over other agents when gout or hyperuricemia is present
rules.mechanism: Losartan, uniquely among ARBs, inhibits the URAT1 urate-anion exchanger in the proximal tubule, increasing urate excretion and lowering serum urate — the exact opposite of the thiazide effect.

effects.estimate_basis: A cited mg/dL figure for losartan's urate-lowering effect could not be retrieved within this session (the delegated agent listed it as an unresolved gap). -0.7 mg/dL is a flagged modelling estimate chosen to roughly offset the HCTZ rise in RX-GOUT-HCTZ so the contrast is visible. SEE C-notes.md gap list before quoting this to anyone.

warning.short: Losartan lowers urate — the anti-thiazide
warning.full: Losartan is the preferred antihypertensive in this five-drug set for a patient with gout or hyperuricemia: it lowers serum urate via URAT1 inhibition, whereas hydrochlorothiazide raises it. This is a losartan-specific property, not an ARB class effect. CONFIDENCE FLAG: the magnitude of the urate reduction is an estimate, not a sourced number — the direction and mechanism are well established, the number is not.

evidence.source: Cochrane review of thiazide metabolic effects — the contrast case (PMID 24869750)
evidence.quote: Thiazides reduced potassium, increased uric acid and increased total cholesterol and triglycerides.

rules.title: Metoprolol succinate ER (not tartrate) in HFrEF
rules.mechanism: Chronic beta-1 blockade reverses catecholamine-driven myocyte toxicity and adverse remodelling, which is why it lowers mortality in HFrEF despite acutely reducing contractility.

provenance.quote: In patients with HFrEF, with current or previous symptoms, use of 1 of the 3 beta blockers proven to reduce mortality (e.g., bisoprolol, carvedilol, sustained-release metoprolol succinate) is recommended to reduce mortality and hospitalizations. (COR 1, LOE A)

provenance.source: FDA label, metoprolol succinate ER §2.3 Heart Failure
provenance.quote: The recommended starting dose of metoprolol succinate extended-release tablets is 25 mg once daily for two weeks in patients with NYHA Class II heart failure and 12.5 mg once daily in patients with more severe heart failure. Double the dose every two weeks to the highest dosage level tolerated by the patient or up to 200 mg.
up to 200 mg of metoprolol succinate extended-release tablets

warning.short: HFrEF — metoprolol SUCCINATE only, start low, double every 2 weeks
warning.full: In HFrEF, only bisoprolol, carvedilol and sustained-release metoprolol succinate are proven to reduce mortality (COR 1, LOE A). AUDIT NOTE, IMPORTANT FOR THIS PRODUCT: metoprolol TARTRATE has no heart failure indication on its FDA label and does not substitute — its indications are hypertension, angina and myocardial infarction only. If the Pills page lets a user compose a metoprolol product, the salt must be modeled, or the simulator will make a clinically false recommendation. Start 25 mg (12.5 mg if more severe), double every two weeks to 200 mg maximum. Never initiate during acute decompensation.

evidence.source: FDA label, metoprolol succinate ER §1.3 and §14.3 (MERIT-HF)
evidence.quote: MERIT-HF was a double-blind, placebo-controlled study of metoprolol succinate extended-release tablets conducted in which 3991 patients with ejection fraction <= 0.40 and NYHA Class II-IV heart failure ... were randomized 1:1 to metoprolol succinate extended-release tablets or placebo.

rules.title: Calcium channel blockers in HFrEF — amlodipine is neutral, not beneficial
rules.mechanism: Dihydropyridine vasodilation does not address the neurohormonal drivers of heart failure progression, so it lowers blood pressure without altering the disease trajectory.

provenance.source: FDA label, amlodipine besylate tablets — PRAISE clinical study description
provenance.quote: There was no statistically significant difference between amlodipine besylate and placebo in the primary endpoint of all-cause mortality (95% confidence limits from 8% reduction to 29% increase on amlodipine besylate). With amlodipine besylate there were more reports of pulmonary edema.
provenance.note: The 1.2 ratio is ESTIMATED - the label reports 'more reports' without a number. Direction is sourced, magnitude is not.

warning.short: Amlodipine is HF-neutral — use it only for another indication
warning.full: Dihydropyridine CCBs including amlodipine are COR 3 (No Benefit), LOE A as heart failure therapy in the 2022 AHA/ACC/HFSA guideline. Amlodipine is mortality-neutral in HFrEF (PRAISE) and is therefore the CCB of choice if one is needed for angina or refractory blood pressure — but it treats neither the heart failure nor its prognosis, and the label notes more reports of pulmonary edema. Non-dihydropyridines (verapamil, diltiazem) are a different matter entirely: COR 3 (Harm), LOE A. AUDIT CORRECTION: the team's draft said verapamil is 'often avoided' — the guideline classifies it as harmful, which is stronger.
